Occupational Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Plan and administer occupational therapy treatments for residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Occupational Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for occupational therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Occupational Therapist as appropriate.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, families, and caregivers.
  • Monitor and document patient responses to treatment interventions.
  • Complete all required documentation and forms in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy Assistant license inFL.
  • Current certification as a Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA).
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

Make a meaningful difference in residents' lives while enjoying the flexibility of a PRN role.Apply today

Nexus at Elmwood Parkhas an exciting opportunity for aFull-time Occupational Therapy Assistant (OTA)inElmwood Park, ILWe are looking for a dedicated OTA to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. AtNexus at Elmwood Park, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Plan and administer occupational therapy treatments for residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Occupational Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for occupational therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Occupational Therapist as appropriate.
  • Ensure all treatment is provided in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, families, and caregivers.
  • Monitor and document patient responses to treatment interventions.
  • Complete all required documentation and forms in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy Assistant license inIL.
  • Current certification as a Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA).
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Full-Time Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate COTA who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Wood Mill, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes true client success over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time COTA, you will be hands-on in helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Treat & Empower: Carry out highly individualized care plans established by the evaluating OT, focusing on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our OTs, PTAs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy Assistant program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state OTA license required.
  • Certification: NBCOT certification is required.

Full-Time Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate COTA who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Meadow View, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes true client success over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time COTA, you will be hands-on in helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Treat & Empower: Carry out highly individualized care plans established by the evaluating OT, focusing on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our OTs, PTAs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy Assistant program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state OTA license required.
  • Certification: NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical execution, empathy, adaptability, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Full-Time Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate COTA who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Norwell Nursing and Rehabilitation Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes true client success over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time COTA, you will be hands-on in helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Treat & Empower: Carry out highly individualized care plans established by the evaluating OT, focusing on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our OTs, PTAs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy Assistant program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state OTA license required.
  • Certification: NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical execution, empathy, adaptability, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.

  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Full-Time Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate COTA who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Norwell Nursing and Rehabilitation Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes true client success over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time COTA, you will be hands-on in helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Treat & Empower: Carry out highly individualized care plans established by the evaluating OT, focusing on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our OTs, PTAs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy Assistant program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state OTA license required.
  • Certification: NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical execution, empathy, adaptability, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you!

Full-Time Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate COTA who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes true client success over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time COTA, you will be hands-on in helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Treat & Empower: Carry out highly individualized care plans established by the evaluating OT, focusing on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our OTs, PTAs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy Assistant program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state OTA license in CT.
  • Certification: NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical execution, empathy, adaptability, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your clinical insights as an assistant are truly valued.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you!

org_desc:
Full-Time Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate COTA who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes true client success over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time COTA, you will be hands-on in helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Treat & Empower: Carry out highly individualized care plans established by the evaluating OT, focusing on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our OTs, PTAs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy Assistant program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state OTA license in CT.
  • Certification: NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical execution, empathy, adaptability, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your clinical insights as an assistant are truly valued.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you!

>

Occupational Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Plan and administer occupational therapy treatments for residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities.

  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, families, and caregivers.
  • Monitor and document patient responses to treatment interventions.
  • Complete all required documentation and forms in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy Assistant license inCT.
  • Current certification as aCertified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA).
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Occupational Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy Assistant license.
  • Current certification as aCertified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA).

  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.

Director of Rehab (DOR) - Lead Our In-House Therapy Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Reclaim Your Career ~Lead With Purpose As Our In-House Rehab Director!

Are you a driven therapy professional who is tired of managing unrealistic productivity metrics and fighting through endless corporate red tape? Are you ready to step into a leadership role where you can actually make a difference?

At Royal Health Wayland, we are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. We are looking for a passionate Director of Rehab to lead our clinical team, foster a positive culture, and drive outstanding patient outcomes. If you want to lead a department that prioritizes holistic care and clinical integration over corporate quotas, we want you at the helm!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our DOR, you will be the captain of our therapy department, balancing clinical excellence with operational success.

  • Lead & Inspire: Manage, mentor, and support a multidisciplinary team of PTs, OTs, SLPs, and assistants, fostering a collaborative and highly engaged work environment.
  • Program Development: Drive clinical programming and community integration initiatives to ensure our patients achieve their highest level of independence.
  • Operations & Compliance: Oversee daily department operations, manage caseloads, and ensure strict compliance with Medicare guidelines, state/federal regulations, and facility protocols.
  • Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Work hand-in-hand with facility leadership, nursing staff, and admissions to ensure seamless patient transitions and top-tier care.
  • Tech & Reporting: Utilize EMR and management systems (experience with platforms like Net Health or PointClickCare is a huge plus!) to track clinical success and department efficiency.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education & Licensure: Active state license as a Physical Therapist (PT), Occupational Therapist (OT), Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP), Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA), or Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA) in MA.
  • Experience: Proven clinical experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting. Previous management or DOR experience is highly preferred.
  • Knowledge: Strong understanding of Medicare regulations, PDPM, and ethical reimbursement practices.
  • Skills: Exceptional leadership capabilities, strategic problem-solving skills, and a genuine passion for staff development and geriatric care.

Why You’ll Love Leading With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in our leaders.

  • Highly Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your leadership and clinical experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical operational standards that allow you to actually support your team.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays so you can recharge.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Empowered Culture: A supportive environment where your operational insights and clinical expertise truly drive the department.

Ready to Lead the Change?

If you are ready to manage a therapy department the way it was meant to be run, we want to meet you!

Send your resume directly to esolang@qrmhealth.com with the subject line: Director of Rehab Wayland - Your Name

Director of Rehab (DOR) - Lead Our In-House Therapy Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Reclaim Your Career ~Lead With Purpose As Our In-House Rehab Director!

Are you a driven therapy professional who is tired of managing unrealistic productivity metrics and fighting through endless corporate red tape? Are you ready to step into a leadership role where you can actually make a difference?

At Royal Health Wayland, we are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. We are looking for a passionate Director of Rehab to lead our clinical team, foster a positive culture, and drive outstanding patient outcomes. If you want to lead a department that prioritizes holistic care and clinical integration over corporate quotas, we want you at the helm!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our DOR, you will be the captain of our therapy department, balancing clinical excellence with operational success.

  • Lead & Inspire: Manage, mentor, and support a multidisciplinary team of PTs, OTs, SLPs, and assistants, fostering a collaborative and highly engaged work environment.
  • Program Development: Drive clinical programming and community integration initiatives to ensure our patients achieve their highest level of independence.
  • Operations & Compliance: Oversee daily department operations, manage caseloads, and ensure strict compliance with Medicare guidelines, state/federal regulations, and facility protocols.
  • Interdisciplinary Collaboration: Work hand-in-hand with facility leadership, nursing staff, and admissions to ensure seamless patient transitions and top-tier care.
  • Tech & Reporting: Utilize EMR and management systems (experience with platforms like Net Health or PointClickCare is a huge plus!) to track clinical success and department efficiency.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education & Licensure: Active state license as a Physical Therapist (PT), Occupational Therapist (OT), Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP), Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA), or Certified Occupational Therapy Assistant (COTA) in MA.
  • Experience: Proven clinical experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting. Previous management or DOR experience is highly preferred.
  • Knowledge: Strong understanding of Medicare regulations, PDPM, and ethical reimbursement practices.
  • Skills: Exceptional leadership capabilities, strategic problem-solving skills, and a genuine passion for staff development and geriatric care.

Why You’ll Love Leading With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in our leaders.

  • Highly Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your leadership and clinical experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical operational standards that allow you to actually support your team.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays so you can recharge.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Empowered Culture: A supportive environment where your operational insights and clinical expertise truly drive the department.

Ready to Lead the Change?

If you are ready to manage a therapy department the way it was meant to be run, we want to meet you!

Job Type: Full-Time

Setting: Skilled Nursing Facility

Schedule: 40 hour/week.

PRN opportunity also available!

Kingwood Rehab & Healthcare Center is excited to offer an opportunity for a Full-Time Occupational Therapist (OT) to join our in-house rehabilitation team. This role is ideal for a clinician who is passionate about delivering high-quality, resident-centered care in a collaborative skilled nursing environment.

Position Overview

As an Occupational Therapist, you will assess and treat residents to improve function, independence, and overall quality of life. This role includes developing evidence-based treatment plans, delivering skilled therapy services, and collaborating closely with the interdisciplinary team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents to determine functional impairments and therapy needs.

  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans focused on ADLs and IADLs.

  • Track progress and modify treatment plans as needed in coordination with the IDT.

  • Recommend adaptive equipment and home modifications to promote independence.

  • Educate patients, caregivers, and families on therapeutic strategies.

  • Ensure accurate, timely documentation per state, federal, and facility guidelines.

  • Participate in team meetings and care planning activities.

  • Adhere to all regulatory and facility policies.

Qualifications

  • Active Texas Occupational Therapist license.

  • In good standing with all applicable licensing boards.

  • SNF or long-term care experience preferred.

  • Familiarity with Net Health is a plus.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

Full-Time Occupational Therapist (OT) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate Occupational Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Wayland, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes true client success over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time OT, you will be the driving force behind helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Evaluate & Treat: Develop and implement highly individualized care plans focused on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy and community integration.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our COTAs, PTs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state OT license required.
  • Certification: NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

Job Type: Full-Time

Setting: Skilled Nursing Facility

Schedule: 40 hour/week.

PRN opportunity also available!

Kingwood Rehab & Healthcare Center is excited to offer an opportunity for a Full-Time Occupational Therapist (OT) to join our in-house rehabilitation team. This role is ideal for a clinician who is passionate about delivering high-quality, resident-centered care in a collaborative skilled nursing environment.

Position Overview

As an Occupational Therapist, you will assess and treat residents to improve function, independence, and overall quality of life. This role includes developing evidence-based treatment plans, delivering skilled therapy services, and collaborating closely with the interdisciplinary team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents to determine functional impairments and therapy needs.

  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans focused on ADLs and IADLs.

  • Track progress and modify treatment plans as needed in coordination with the IDT.

  • Recommend adaptive equipment and home modifications to promote independence.

  • Educate patients, caregivers, and families on therapeutic strategies.

  • Ensure accurate, timely documentation per state, federal, and facility guidelines.

  • Participate in team meetings and care planning activities.

  • Adhere to all regulatory and facility policies.

Qualifications

  • Active Texas Occupational Therapist license.

  • In good standing with all applicable licensing boards.

  • SNF or long-term care experience preferred.

  • Familiarity with Net Health is a plus.

  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate Occupational Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Wayland, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes true client success over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time OT, you will be the driving force behind helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Evaluate & Treat: Develop and implement highly individualized care plans focused on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy and community integration.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our COTAs, PTs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state OT license required.
  • Certification: NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you!

Occupational Therapist (OT) - Float Position

Job Summary

Nexus is seeking a compassionate and dedicated Occupational Therapist (OT) for a Float Position supporting our rehabilitation teams across the.

This is an excellent opportunity for an OT who enjoys variety, collaboration, and making a meaningful difference across multiple skilled nursing and rehabilitation settings. The Float Occupational Therapist will provide high-quality, patient-centered occupational therapy services based on the needs of each facility.

The ideal candidate is flexible, dependable, clinically confident, and comfortable working with residents across different rehabilitation environments.

Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and develop individualized occupational therapy treatment plans.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy services in accordance with physician orders and established treatment plans.
  • Address deficits related to activities of daily living, functional mobility, strength, coordination, balance, cognition, and upper-extremity function.
  • Provide therapeutic activities and interventions designed to improve residents' independence and safety.
  • Assist residents with dressing, grooming, bathing, toileting, feeding, transfers, and other activities of daily living as appropriate.
  • Provide adaptive equipment recommendations and training when clinically indicated.
  • Educate residents, families, and caregivers regarding safety, functional strategies, home programs, and adaptive techniques.
  • Monitor resident progress and modify treatment plans as clinically appropriate.
  • Complete accurate and timely documentation of evaluations, treatments, progress, and resident responses.
  • Communicate resident progress and changes in condition with the interdisciplinary care team.
  • Collaborate with physical therapists, speech language pathologists, nursing staff, physicians, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Participate in care plan meetings and discharge planning as appropriate.
  • Maintain compliance with federal, state, facility, and professional standards.
  • Adapt effectively to the needs, workflow, and census of each assigned facility.
  • Provide compassionate, respectful, and resident-centered care across all locations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's, Master's, or Doctoral degree in Occupational Therapy from an accredited program, as applicable.
  • Current Illinois Occupational Therapist license required.
  • Skilled nursing, long-term care, subacute rehabilitation, or geriatric experience preferred.
  • Strong clinical assessment and treatment skills.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively within multiple interdisciplinary teams.
  • Flexible and dependable with the ability to travel between assigned locations.
  • Compassionate, professional, and resident-focused approach to care.

Position Details

  • Position Type: Full-Time Float
  • Locations Supported:
  • Setting: Skilled Nursing & Rehabilitation
  • Schedule: Full-time; schedule may vary based on facility needs and census
  • Travel: Local travel between assigned Nexus facilities is required

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance for eligible employees
  • Paid time off
  • Continuing education opportunities
  • Professional growth opportunities
  • Supportive interdisciplinary rehabilitation teams
  • Variety and flexibility across multiple rehabilitation settings

Why Join Our Float Team?

A Float Occupational Therapist position provides the opportunity to work across multiple locations, collaborate with diverse rehabilitation teams, and make an impact where your clinical expertise is needed most.

If you are a flexible and motivated Occupational Therapist looking for a rewarding opportunity serving residents throughout the, we encourage you to apply today!

Join the Nexus rehabilitation team and help residents achieve greater independence, safety, and quality of life.

Occupational Therapist (OT) - Float Position

Job Summary

Nexus is seeking a compassionate and dedicated Occupational Therapist (OT) for a Float Position supporting our rehabilitation teams across the.

This is an excellent opportunity for an OT who enjoys variety, collaboration, and making a meaningful difference across multiple skilled nursing and rehabilitation settings. The Float Occupational Therapist will provide high-quality, patient-centered occupational therapy services based on the needs of each facility.

The ideal candidate is flexible, dependable, clinically confident, and comfortable working with residents across different rehabilitation environments.

Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and develop individualized occupational therapy treatment plans.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy services in accordance with physician orders and established treatment plans.
  • Address deficits related to activities of daily living, functional mobility, strength, coordination, balance, cognition, and upper-extremity function.
  • Provide therapeutic activities and interventions designed to improve residents' independence and safety.
  • Assist residents with dressing, grooming, bathing, toileting, feeding, transfers, and other activities of daily living as appropriate.
  • Provide adaptive equipment recommendations and training when clinically indicated.
  • Educate residents, families, and caregivers regarding safety, functional strategies, home programs, and adaptive techniques.
  • Monitor resident progress and modify treatment plans as clinically appropriate.
  • Complete accurate and timely documentation of evaluations, treatments, progress, and resident responses.
  • Communicate resident progress and changes in condition with the interdisciplinary care team.
  • Collaborate with physical therapists, speech language pathologists, nursing staff, physicians, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Participate in care plan meetings and discharge planning as appropriate.
  • Maintain compliance with federal, state, facility, and professional standards.
  • Adapt effectively to the needs, workflow, and census of each assigned facility.
  • Provide compassionate, respectful, and resident-centered care across all locations.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's, Master's, or Doctoral degree in Occupational Therapy from an accredited program, as applicable.
  • Current Illinois Occupational Therapist license required.
  • Skilled nursing, long-term care, subacute rehabilitation, or geriatric experience preferred.
  • Strong clinical assessment and treatment skills.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work independently and effectively within multiple interdisciplinary teams.
  • Flexible and dependable with the ability to travel between assigned locations.
  • Compassionate, professional, and resident-focused approach to care.

Position Details

  • Position Type: Full-Time Float
  • Locations Supported:
  • Setting: Skilled Nursing & Rehabilitation
  • Schedule: Full-time; schedule may vary based on facility needs and census
  • Travel: Local travel between assigned Nexus facilities is required

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance for eligible employees
  • Paid time off
  • Continuing education opportunities
  • Professional growth opportunities
  • Supportive interdisciplinary rehabilitation teams
  • Variety and flexibility across multiple rehabilitation settings

Why Join Our Float Team?

A Float Occupational Therapist position provides the opportunity to work across multiple locations, collaborate with diverse rehabilitation teams, and make an impact where your clinical expertise is needed most.

If you are a flexible and motivated Occupational Therapist looking for a rewarding opportunity serving residents throughout the, we encourage you to apply today!

Join the Nexus rehabilitation team and help residents achieve greater independence, safety, and quality of life.

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply

We are looking for a dedicated OT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.At Nexus at Berwyn, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.

  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.

  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license .
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply

Part-time/PRN Occupational Therapist (OT) - In-House Rehab Team

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time OT, you will be the driving force behind helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Develop and implement highly individualized care plans focused on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate:Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy and community integration.
  • Collaborate:Work hand-in-hand with our COTAs, PTs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate:Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state OT license in Iowa.
  • Certification:NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you

Occupational Therapist

Nexus at Geneva has an exciting opportunity for a Occupational Therapist (OT)

We are looking for a dedicated OT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.At Nexus at Geneva, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inIL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.

Part-time/PRN Occupational Therapist (OT) - In-House Rehab Team

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time OT, you will be the driving force behind helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Develop and implement highly individualized care plans focused on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate:Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy and community integration.
  • Collaborate:Work hand-in-hand with our COTAs, PTs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate:Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state OT license in Iowa.
  • Certification:NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Part-time/PRN Occupational Therapist (OT) - In-House Rehab Team

Cedar Rapids, IA

Position:Part-time or PRN

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

AtNorthbrook Manor Care Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work

What You'll Be Doing:

As our full-time OT, you will be the driving force behind helping our residents regain their independence and confidently transition back to their daily lives.

  • Evaluate & Treat:Develop and implement highly individualized care plans focused on restoring function in Activities of Daily Living (ADLs) and Instrumental Activities of Daily Living (IADLs).
  • Innovate:Utilize evidence-based practices for cognitive rehabilitation, vision therapy, and adaptive equipment training to maximize patient autonomy and community integration.
  • Collaborate:Work hand-in-hand with our COTAs, PTs, SLPs, and nursing staff to ensure a seamless, patient-centered approach to rehab.
  • Educate:Empower patients, families, and facility staff with strategies to support long-term recovery and safe transitions.
  • Document:Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education:Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.
  • Licensure:Active (or pending) state OT license in Iowa.
  • Certification:NBCOT certification is required.
  • Experience:Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills:Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary:Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations:Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Culture:A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you

Heather Hill Nursing Center has an exciting opportunity for a Occupational Therapist (OT)

We are looking for a dedicated OT to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.At Heather Hill Nursing Center, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today

Occupational Therapist Responsibilities

  • Consult with residents and patients to understand their individual needs, concerns, functional limitations, and rehabilitation goals.
  • Perform comprehensive occupational therapy evaluations and assess and interpret evaluation findings and test results.
  • Develop individualized treatment plans based on evaluation findings, physician orders, patient needs, and established standards of care.
  • Create and implement personalized rehabilitation programs designed to improve functional independence, safety, mobility, and quality of life.
  • Provide skilled occupational therapy interventions to address activities of daily living (ADLs), functional mobility, strength, coordination, cognition, balance, and other areas of occupational performance.
  • Administer medically necessary occupational therapy treatments in accordance with the established plan of care.
  • Monitor resident and patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate.
  • Establish and update individualized goals based on patient progress, functional needs, and clinical findings.
  • Provide education, training, and support to residents, patients, families, and caregivers regarding treatment plans, adaptive techniques, safety, and strategies to promote independence.
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, therapy team members, and other members of the interdisciplinary team (IDT) to coordinate and promote quality patient care.
  • Supervise and provide guidance to Occupational Therapy Assistants in accordance with applicable regulations and professional standards.
  • Communicate changes in resident or patient condition, progress, and treatment needs to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Maintain accurate records related to evaluations, treatment sessions, progress, goals, and discharge planning.
  • Comply with all applicable rules, regulations, policies, procedures, and professional standards.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Occupational Therapist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of occupational therapy treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with residents and patients with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, therapy team members, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Strong understanding of functional assessment, rehabilitation, and strategies to promote independence.

Occupational Therapist Requirements

  • Active and valid Occupational Therapy license inFL.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.
  • Graduate of an accredited Occupational Therapy program.

Career Advantages

  • Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

All inquiries will be kept confidential.
