Full-Time Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate Physical Therapist Assistant who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Meadow View, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time PTA, you will be on the front lines of restoring mobility, strength, and confidence for our residents.

  • Treat & Empower: Implement targeted, evidence-based treatment plans designed by the evaluating PT to address mobility, balance, gait, and pain management.
  • Innovate: Carry out specialized programs (like fall prevention and joint replacement recovery) to ensure our patients achieve their highest possible level of independence and success.
  • Collaborate: Partner seamlessly with our PTs, alongside COTAs, SLPs, and nursing teams, to deliver cohesive and comprehensive clinical care.
  • Educate: Empower patients and their families with the physical tools and knowledge needed for safe discharges and active community integration.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapist Assistant program.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state PTA license required.
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is highly preferred, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical execution, empathy, adaptability, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you!

Culver West Health Center has an amazing opportunity for a Full Time Physical Therapy Assistant (PTA) to join their In-House Therapy Team. We are a 91-bed skilled nursing and rehabilitation center in Culver City, California. We have been providing specialized therapy services and skilled nursing care to our community for over 40 years.

At Culver West Health Center, caring is our main concern. Our organization is built on the premise that the most effective way to provide compassionate care is to:

  • Maintain high medical integrity
  • Foster a team spirit among staff
  • Create friendly, beautiful surroundings for our patients and their visitors

Our team of qualified professionals helps patients recover from surgery, injury, or serious illness. We understand the importance of creating a comfortable and nurturing atmosphere, whether patients stay for short-term treatment or long-term care.

To provide the best quality of care, our trained staff will provide customized care programs for each of our residents, ensuring them the most successful outcomes.

We know that the transition to a skilled nursing facility is challenging. At Culver West Health Center, we strive to ease the process by providing an environment where patients and guests feel informed and comfortable.

Each patient will be paired with a coordinator to help ease the transition and provide a familiar smiling face. Our staff is here to answer any of your questions and lend a helping hand.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

  • Administer treatment to residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities to relieve pain, restore or improve function, and promote healing
  • Assure all treatment is delivered in accordance with an established plan of care
  • Provide clinical support and instruct patients, families, and caregivers
  • Monitor patient response to treatment intervention
  • Complete required forms and documentation in accordance with company policy and state/federal regulations
  • Consulting with patients to learn about their physical condition.
  • Assessing and interpreting patient evaluations and test results.
  • Developing treatment plans using a variety of treatment techniques.
  • Creating personalized fitness-oriented health care programs for patients.
  • Administering medically prescribed physical therapy treatments to relieve pain and improve mobility.
  • Advising patients on exercise techniques.
  • Advising patients and their families about in-home treatment options.
  • Providing educational information about injury prevention, ergonomics and ways to promote physical health.
  • Consulting and collaborating with other healthcare professionals.
  • Documenting patient care history.
  • Complying with rules, regulations, and procedures.

Career Advantages:

  • In-house opportunity
  • Practice in an environment built on integrity and progressive, ethical care
  • Clinical expertise & training available
  • Electronic documentation system
  • Work collaboratively with a supportive team of therapists and nursing staff
  • Flexible Schedule

Benefits

  • Medical Benefits
  • Dental
  • Vision
  • PTO

St. Patrick's Manor Nursing & Rosarie Center has an exciting opportunity available for a Full-time and PRN Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) to join the new in-house therapy team!

St. Patrick's Manor is a nonprofit, short-term and long-term care facility. Our peaceful, home-like setting makes St. Patrick's Manor the perfect choice for all care needs. For over 7 decades, individuals, families and physicians have been choosing and recommending St. Patrick's Manor for it's upcompromising commitment to excellence.

Our community is known for providing exceptional care. Our professional and dedicated staff provides occupational, physical and speech therapy on a daily full-time basis. Treatment programs are designed to meet the physical and emotional goals necessary for residents to reach their optimum levels of functioning. A warm welcome and creative approach in treatment is the core of the motivation spirit that is generated within the rehabilitation department.

Responsibilities:

  • Administer treatment to residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities to relieve pain, restore or improve function, and promote healing
  • Assure all treatment is delivered in accordance with an established plan of care
  • Provide clinical support and instruct patients, families, and caregivers
  • Monitor patient response to treatment intervention
  • Complete required forms and documentation in accordance with company policy and state/federal regulations
  • Consulting with patients to learn about their physical condition.
  • Assessing and interpreting patient evaluations and test results.
  • Developing treatment plans using a variety of treatment techniques.
  • Creating personalized fitness-oriented health care programs for patients.
  • Administering medically prescribed physical therapy treatments to relieve pain and improve mobility.
  • Advising patients on exercise techniques.
  • Advising patients and their families about in-home treatment options.
  • Providing educational information about injury prevention, ergonomics and ways to promote physical health.
  • Consulting and collaborating with other healthcare professionals.
  • Documenting patient care history.
  • Complying with rules, regulations, and procedures.

Qualifications

  • Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapist Assistant program.
  • Current state PTA license in good standing.
  • CPR/BLS certification (required).
  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing or subacute rehab setting preferred.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.

  • Practice in an environment built on integrity and progressive, ethical care

Physical Therapy Assistant (Full-Time)

A Full-Time Physical Therapist Assistant PTA is needed at Avir at Moody in Fairfield, TX!

We are looking for a dedicated PTA to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

At Avir at Moody, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today!

Physical Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Administer physical therapy treatments designed to relieve pain, improve or restore function, and promote healing.
  • Provide skilled physical therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Physical Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for physical therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Physical Therapist as appropriate.
  • Implement the patient's physical therapy plan of treatment under the supervision and direction of the Physical Therapist.
  • Measure and document patient progress related to motor function, strength, mobility, and muscle performance.
  • Monitor patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate, in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team (IDT) and supervising Physical Therapist.
  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, family members, and caregivers in collaboration with the Physical Therapist.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Physical Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of physical therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with Physical Therapists and the interdisciplinary team.

Physical Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Physical Therapy Assistant license in TX.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-Time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply!
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

Physical Therapy Assistant (Full-Time)

A Full-Time Physical Therapist Assistant PTA is needed at Avir at Moody in Fairfield, TX!

We are looking for a dedicated PTA to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. Our goal is to help each individual achieve meaningful outcomes while maintaining the highest standards of quality and compassion.

At Avir at Moody, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Our staff works together to develop customized treatment programs and best practices designed to meet the unique needs of each resident and exceed industry standards.

Don't wait to make a difference-apply today!

Physical Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Administer physical therapy treatments designed to relieve pain, improve or restore function, and promote healing.
  • Provide skilled physical therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Physical Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for physical therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Physical Therapist as appropriate.
  • Implement the patient's physical therapy plan of treatment under the supervision and direction of the Physical Therapist.
  • Measure and document patient progress related to motor function, strength, mobility, and muscle performance.
  • Monitor patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate, in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team (IDT) and supervising Physical Therapist.
  • Provide clinical support and education to patients, family members, and caregivers in collaboration with the Physical Therapist.
  • Ensure all documentation is completed accurately, thoroughly, and in a timely manner in accordance with company policies and applicable state and federal regulations.
  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Physical Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of physical therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with Physical Therapists and the interdisciplinary team.

Physical Therapy Assistant Requirements

  • Active and valid Physical Therapy Assistant license in TX.
  • Must be in good standing with all applicable regulatory agencies and licensing boards.

Career Advantages

  • Full-Time Opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates welcome to apply!
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive, collaborative clinical environment
  • Opportunity to make a meaningful difference in the lives of our residents and patients

St. Patrick's Manor Nursing & Rosarie Center has an exciting opportunity available for a Full-time and PRN Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) to join the new in-house therapy team!

St. Patrick's Manor is a nonprofit, short-term and long-term care facility. Our peaceful, home-like setting makes St. Patrick's Manor the perfect choice for all care needs. For over 7 decades, individuals, families and physicians have been choosing and recommending St. Patrick's Manor for it's upcompromising commitment to excellence.

Our community is known for providing exceptional care. Our professional and dedicated staff provides occupational, physical and speech therapy on a daily full-time basis. Treatment programs are designed to meet the physical and emotional goals necessary for residents to reach their optimum levels of functioning. A warm welcome and creative approach in treatment is the core of the motivation spirit that is generated within the rehabilitation department.

Responsibilities:

  • Administer treatment to residents and patients with temporary or long-term disabilities to relieve pain, restore or improve function, and promote healing
  • Assure all treatment is delivered in accordance with an established plan of care
  • Provide clinical support and instruct patients, families, and caregivers
  • Monitor patient response to treatment intervention
  • Complete required forms and documentation in accordance with company policy and state/federal regulations
  • Consulting with patients to learn about their physical condition.
  • Assessing and interpreting patient evaluations and test results.
  • Developing treatment plans using a variety of treatment techniques.
  • Creating personalized fitness-oriented health care programs for patients.
  • Administering medically prescribed physical therapy treatments to relieve pain and improve mobility.
  • Advising patients on exercise techniques.
  • Advising patients and their families about in-home treatment options.
  • Providing educational information about injury prevention, ergonomics and ways to promote physical health.
  • Consulting and collaborating with other healthcare professionals.
  • Documenting patient care history.
  • Complying with rules, regulations, and procedures.

Qualifications

  • Graduate of an accredited Physical Therapist Assistant program.
  • Current state PTA license in good standing.
  • CPR/BLS certification (required).
  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing or subacute rehab setting preferred.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills.

Career Advantages:

  • In-House opportunity
  • Practice in an environment built on integrity and progressive, ethical care
  • Clinical expertise & training available
  • Electronic documentation system
  • Work collaboratively with a supportive team of therapists and nursing staff

Benefits:

  • PTO

  • Attend required meetings and participate in other duties as designated by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Physical Therapy Assistant Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of physical therapy treatment practices and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system preferred.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.
  • Commitment to providing compassionate, patient-centered care.
  • Ability to work collaboratively with Physical Therapists and the interdisciplinary team.

  • Active and valid Physical Therapy Assistant license inTX.

  • Implement the patient's physical therapy plan of treatment under the supervision and direction of the Physical Therapist.

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting preferred.
  • Current knowledge of physical therapy treatment practices and interventions.

  • Ability to effectively work with patients and residents with a variety of personalities, needs, and abilities.

St. Patrick's Manor Nursing & Rosarie Center has an exciting opportunity for a Full-Time Physical Therapy Assistant (PTA)

We are looking for a dedicated PTA to join our in-house rehabilitation team of outstanding professionals who provide person-centered care to our residents and patients. At St. Patrick's Manor Nursing & Rosarie Center, our clinical teams are committed to providing individualized care with compassion, collaboration, and excellence. Physical Therapy Assistant Responsibilities

  • Administer physical therapy treatments designed to relieve pain, improve or restore function, and promote healing.
  • Provide skilled physical therapy services and interventions in accordance with physician orders and under the supervision of a licensed Physical Therapist.
  • Respond to requests for physical therapy services by communicating relevant information and making referrals to the Physical Therapist as appropriate.
  • Implement the patient's physical therapy plan of treatment under the supervision and direction of the Physical Therapist.
  • Measure and document patient progress related to motor function, strength, mobility, and muscle performance.
  • Monitor patient responses to treatment interventions and modify treatment approaches as clinically appropriate, in collaboration with the interdisciplinary team (IDT) and supervising Physical Therapist.

Setting:In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout

Why You'll Love Working With Us (The Perks):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate Speech-Language Pathologist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Middletown Nursing and Rehab Center, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time SLP, you will be the cornerstone of our speech, swallowing, and cognitive therapy programs.

  • Evaluate & Treat: Provide comprehensive assessments and individualized treatment plans for speech, language, cognitive-communication, and swallowing disorders (dysphagia).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices to help our residents regain independence and improve their quality of life.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our PTs, OTs, nursing staff, and dietary team to ensure holistic, patient-centered care.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with the knowledge and strategies they need to support recovery.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Master’s Degree in Speech-Language Pathology.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state SLP license required.
  • Certification: Certificate of Clinical Competence (ASHA CCC-SLP) is highly preferred. (Strong CFYs with a passion for adult/geriatric rehab will be considered!)
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you!

Full-Time Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) - In-House Rehab Team!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate Speech-Language Pathologist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Meadow View, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time SLP, you will be the cornerstone of our speech, swallowing, and cognitive therapy programs.

  • Evaluate & Treat: Provide comprehensive assessments and individualized treatment plans for speech, language, cognitive-communication, and swallowing disorders (dysphagia).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices to help our residents regain independence and improve their quality of life.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our PTs, OTs, nursing staff, and dietary team to ensure holistic, patient-centered care.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with the knowledge and strategies they need to support recovery.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Master’s Degree in Speech-Language Pathology.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state SLP license required.
  • Certification: Certificate of Clinical Competence (ASHA CCC-SLP) is highly preferred. (Strong CFYs with a passion for adult/geriatric rehab will be considered!)
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you!

Speech Language Pathologist (SLP) - In-House Subacute Rehabilitation

Nexus at Elmwood Park

Job Type: Full-Time / Part-Time

Setting: In-House Subacute Rehabilitation & Skilled Nursing

Job Summary

Nexus at Elmwood Park is seeking a compassionate and motivated Speech Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our in-house rehabilitation team in Elmwood Park, Illinois. The ideal candidate will evaluate and treat residents with speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing disorders in a subacute rehabilitation and skilled nursing setting.

This position offers the opportunity to work collaboratively with an interdisciplinary team dedicated to helping patients regain independence and improve quality of life.

Responsibilities

  • Evaluate, diagnose, and develop individualized treatment plans for residents with speech, language, cognitive, voice, and swallowing disorders
  • Provide skilled speech therapy services in accordance with physician orders and facility policies
  • Perform clinical swallowing evaluations and dysphagia treatment
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation in compliance with state, federal, and facility guidelines
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, occupational therapists, physical therapists, and families regarding patient progress and discharge planning
  • Educate patients, caregivers, and staff on communication and swallowing strategies
  • Participate in care plan meetings and interdisciplinary team discussions
  • Ensure compliance with all regulatory and ethical standards

Qualifications

  • Master’s Degree in Speech Language Pathology
  • Current Illinois SLP license required
  • Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC-SLP) preferred
  • Experience in skilled nursing, subacute rehabilitation, or geriatric settings preferred
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Continuing education opportunities
  • Supportive in-house therapy team
  • Flexible scheduling options

Why Join Us?

Join a collaborative in-house rehabilitation team focused on delivering high-quality patient-centered care in a supportive and professional environment. We value clinical excellence, teamwork, and compassionate care.

Apply today to become part of our growing rehabilitation team at Nexus at Elmwood Park!

Forest Manor Health & Rehab Center is seeking a dedicated and compassionate Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our skilled rehabilitation team. We currently have openings for both Full-Time and Per Diem (PRN) positions.

Nexus at Elmwood Park

Job Type: Full-Time / Part-Time

Setting: In-House Subacute Rehabilitation & Skilled Nursing

Job Summary

Nexus at Elmwood Park is seeking a compassionate and motivated Speech Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our in-house rehabilitation team in Elmwood Park, Illinois. The ideal candidate will evaluate and treat residents with speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing disorders in a subacute rehabilitation and skilled nursing setting.

This position offers the opportunity to work collaboratively with an interdisciplinary team dedicated to helping patients regain independence and improve quality of life.

Responsibilities

  • Evaluate, diagnose, and develop individualized treatment plans for residents with speech, language, cognitive, voice, and swallowing disorders
  • Provide skilled speech therapy services in accordance with physician orders and facility policies
  • Perform clinical swallowing evaluations and dysphagia treatment
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation in compliance with state, federal, and facility guidelines
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, occupational therapists, physical therapists, and families regarding patient progress and discharge planning
  • Educate patients, caregivers, and staff on communication and swallowing strategies
  • Participate in care plan meetings and interdisciplinary team discussions
  • Ensure compliance with all regulatory and ethical standards

Qualifications

  • Master’s Degree in Speech Language Pathology
  • Current Illinois SLP license required
  • Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC-SLP) preferred
  • Experience in skilled nursing, subacute rehabilitation, or geriatric settings preferred
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Continuing education opportunities
  • Supportive in-house therapy team
  • Flexible scheduling options

Why Join Us?

Join a collaborative in-house rehabilitation team focused on delivering high-quality patient-centered care in a supportive and professional environment. We value clinical excellence, teamwork, and compassionate care.

Apply today to become part of our growing rehabilitation team at Nexus at Elmwood Park!

Position: Full-Time (FT)

Setting: In-House Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF)

Say Goodbye to Contract Company Burnout!

Are you a passionate Speech-Language Pathologist who loves working with the geriatric population but is tired of unrealistic productivity metrics and endless corporate red tape?

At Royal Meadow View, we do things differently. We are proud to operate a 100% in-house therapy department. That means you work directly for our facility, collaborating closely with a dedicated interdisciplinary team that prioritizes patient outcomes over corporate quotas. Come build meaningful relationships with your patients and actually enjoy going to work!

What You’ll Be Doing:

As our full-time SLP, you will be the cornerstone of our speech, swallowing, and cognitive therapy programs.

  • Evaluate & Treat: Provide comprehensive assessments and individualized treatment plans for speech, language, cognitive-communication, and swallowing disorders (dysphagia).
  • Innovate: Utilize evidence-based practices to help our residents regain independence and improve their quality of life.
  • Collaborate: Work hand-in-hand with our PTs, OTs, nursing staff, and dietary team to ensure holistic, patient-centered care.
  • Educate: Empower patients, families, and facility staff with the knowledge and strategies they need to support recovery.
  • Document: Maintain accurate, timely clinical documentation in accordance with state, federal, and facility guidelines.

What You Bring to the Table:

  • Education: Master’s Degree in Speech-Language Pathology.
  • Licensure: Active (or pending) state SLP license required.
  • Certification: Certificate of Clinical Competence (ASHA CCC-SLP) is highly preferred. (Strong CFYs with a passion for adult/geriatric rehab will be considered!)
  • Experience: Previous experience in a SNF or adult rehab setting is a plus, but a collaborative mindset and passion for patient care are what matter most.
  • Skills: Strong clinical reasoning, empathy, and excellent communication skills.

Why You’ll Love Working With Us (The Perks!):

Because we are in-house, we invest directly in YOU.

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience.
  • Realistic Expectations: Ethical, manageable productivity standards.
  • Comprehensive Health Benefits: Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance.
  • Generous PTO: Paid time off and paid holidays to support your work-life balance.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan.
  • Culture: A supportive, family-like environment where your voice actually matters.

Ready to Make a Difference?

If you are ready to practice therapy the way it was meant to be practiced, we want to meet you!

Speech Language Pathologist (SLP) - In-House Subacute Rehabilitation

Nexus at Elmwood Park

Job Type: Full-Time / Part-Time

Setting: In-House Subacute Rehabilitation & Skilled Nursing

Job Summary

Nexus at Elmwood Park is seeking a compassionate and motivated Speech Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our in-house rehabilitation team in Elmwood Park, Illinois. The ideal candidate will evaluate and treat residents with speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing disorders in a subacute rehabilitation and skilled nursing setting.

This position offers the opportunity to work collaboratively with an interdisciplinary team dedicated to helping patients regain independence and improve quality of life.

Responsibilities

  • Evaluate, diagnose, and develop individualized treatment plans for residents with speech, language, cognitive, voice, and swallowing disorders
  • Provide skilled speech therapy services in accordance with physician orders and facility policies
  • Perform clinical swallowing evaluations and dysphagia treatment
  • Maintain accurate and timely documentation in compliance with state, federal, and facility guidelines
  • Collaborate with physicians, nursing staff, occupational therapists, physical therapists, and families regarding patient progress and discharge planning
  • Educate patients, caregivers, and staff on communication and swallowing strategies
  • Participate in care plan meetings and interdisciplinary team discussions
  • Ensure compliance with all regulatory and ethical standards

Qualifications

  • Master’s Degree in Speech Language Pathology
  • Current Illinois SLP license required
  • Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC-SLP) preferred
  • Experience in skilled nursing, subacute rehabilitation, or geriatric settings preferred
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team

Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance
  • Paid time off
  • Continuing education opportunities
  • Supportive in-house therapy team
  • Flexible scheduling options

Why Join Us?

Join a collaborative in-house rehabilitation team focused on delivering high-quality patient-centered care in a supportive and professional environment. We value clinical excellence, teamwork, and compassionate care.

Apply today to become part of our growing rehabilitation team at Nexus at Elmwood Park!

Riviera Healthcare Center actively seeking a Full Time Speech Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our in-house therapy team for 35-40 hours/week! CFs are welcomed!

Welcome to Riviera Healthcare Center. We are committed to being a leader in the skilled nursing and rehabilitation arena. For over 50 years, our 150-bed facility has been providing the highest quality nursing and rehabilitation services to our residents.

Areas of treatment focus may include:

  • Improving speech and voice clarity
  • Increasing comprehension and verbal expression
  • Improving chewing and swallowing ability
  • Maximizing cognitive language skills: memory, problem-solving, and abstract reasoning
  • Resident and family/caregiver education and training for managing ongoing difficulties with communication, cognition, and swallowing

Responsibilities:

  • Evaluate Residents conditions for swallowing or cognitive deficits
  • Help Residents in their goals to improve Cognition of Swallowing
  • Education for Residents and Caregivers
  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech and language therapy assessments as well as develop and implement individualized treatment plans to increase client's independence and functioning
  • Provide augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems for individuals with severe expressive and/or language comprehension disorders
  • Provide training and education to client, family, caregivers and other professionals as a subject matter expert
  • Coordinate and collaborate with other professionals for diagnostic swallowing procedures (MBSS, FEES) as ordered by physician
  • Demonstrate competent technical skills according to current Speech Therapy standards of practice
  • Communicate changes in resident's condition
  • Provide accurate and timely billing records and supporting clinical documentation
  • Respond to family requests and concerns timely
  • Coordinate and provide training with Restorative Nursing and other Care staff
  • Assure resident abuse or neglect does not occur
  • Observe confidentiality and safeguards for all patient information
  • Complies with federal, state, and local legal and professional requirements

Career Advantages:

  • In-House opportunity
  • Practice in an environment built on integrity and progressive, ethical care
  • Clinical expertise & training available
  • Electronic documentation system
  • Work collaboratively with a supportive team of therapists and nursing staff
  • Flexible schedule
  • Full Benefits/PTO

Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Speech-Language Pathology or equivalent
  • Valid state licensure as a Speech-Language Pathologist
  • Proficient in speech therapy techniques and patient assessment
  • Strong knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and medical terminology
  • Experience working with patients with dysphagia
  • Excellent communication and patient care skills

As an SLP, you will evaluate, diagnose, and treat residents with communication, cognitive-linguistic, and swallowing disorders. You will work closely with an interdisciplinary team to help residents regain their independence and improve their quality of life.

  • Conduct evaluations and develop individualized treatment plans for residents with speech, language, cognitive, and swallowing disorders.

  • Master's degree in Speech-Language Pathology from an accredited program.

Riviera Healthcare Center actively seeking a Full Time Speech Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our in-house therapy team for 35-40 hours/week! CFs are welcomed!

Welcome to Riviera Healthcare Center. We are committed to being a leader in the skilled nursing and rehabilitation arena. For over 50 years, our 150-bed facility has been providing the highest quality nursing and rehabilitation services to our residents.

Areas of treatment focus may include:

  • Improving speech and voice clarity
  • Increasing comprehension and verbal expression
  • Improving chewing and swallowing ability
  • Maximizing cognitive language skills: memory, problem-solving, and abstract reasoning
  • Resident and family/caregiver education and training for managing ongoing difficulties with communication, cognition, and swallowing

Responsibilities:

  • Evaluate Residents conditions for swallowing or cognitive deficits
  • Help Residents in their goals to improve Cognition of Swallowing
  • Education for Residents and Caregivers
  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech and language therapy assessments as well as develop and implement individualized treatment plans to increase client's independence and functioning
  • Provide augmentative and alternative communication (AAC) systems for individuals with severe expressive and/or language comprehension disorders
  • Provide training and education to client, family, caregivers and other professionals as a subject matter expert
  • Coordinate and collaborate with other professionals for diagnostic swallowing procedures (MBSS, FEES) as ordered by physician
  • Demonstrate competent technical skills according to current Speech Therapy standards of practice
  • Communicate changes in resident's condition
  • Provide accurate and timely billing records and supporting clinical documentation
  • Respond to family requests and concerns timely
  • Coordinate and provide training with Restorative Nursing and other Care staff
  • Assure resident abuse or neglect does not occur
  • Observe confidentiality and safeguards for all patient information
  • Complies with federal, state, and local legal and professional requirements

Career Advantages:

  • In-House opportunity
  • Practice in an environment built on integrity and progressive, ethical care
  • Clinical expertise & training available
  • Electronic documentation system
  • Work collaboratively with a supportive team of therapists and nursing staff
  • Flexible schedule
  • Full Benefits/PTO

Qualifications

  • Master's degree in Speech-Language Pathology or equivalent
  • Valid state licensure as a Speech-Language Pathologist
  • Proficient in speech therapy techniques and patient assessment
  • Strong knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and medical terminology
  • Experience working with patients with dysphagia
  • Excellent communication and patient care skills

  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.

  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.

Speech-Language Pathologist

New Carlton Rehabilitation & Nursing Centerhas an exciting opportunity for a Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP)to join our team

We're looking for a dedicated and compassionate SLP to join our in-house rehabilitation team and provide high-quality, person-centered care to our residents and patients. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside an experienced clinical team focused on helping each individual reach meaningful goals and maintain the highest level of independence possible.

AtNew Carlton Rehabilitation & Nursing Center, our rehabilitation team valuescompassion, collaboration, and clinical excellence. We work together to create individualized treatment plans and provide care that meets the unique needs of each resident and patient.

If you're looking for a supportive team where your clinical expertise can make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and patients for speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans focused on cognition, communication, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech-language pathology services in accordance with established plans of care.
  • Help residents and patients achieve their individualized cognitive, communication, and swallowing goals.
  • Provide education, training, and support for residents, families, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals regarding diagnostic swallowing procedures, including Modified Barium Swallow Studies (MBSS) and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES), as ordered and clinically indicated.
  • Apply sound clinical judgment and maintain skills consistent with current speech-language pathology standards of practice.
  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Speech-Language Pathologist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and patients with a variety of needs, abilities, and personalities.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, and the interdisciplinary team.
  • A genuine commitment to compassionate, patient-centered care.

Speech-Language Pathologist Requirements

  • Active and valid Speech-Language Pathology license .
  • Current ASHA certification.
  • Must be in good standing with applicable licensing boards and regulatory agencies.

  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates are welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive and collaborative clinical environment

Riviera Healthcare Center has an exciting opportunity for a Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP)to join our team

Please change to FT

We're looking for a dedicated and compassionate SLP to join our in-house rehabilitation team and provide high-quality, person-centered care to our residents and patients. You'll have the opportunity to work alongside an experienced clinical team focused on helping each individual reach meaningful goals and maintain the highest level of independence possible.

At Riviera Healthcare Center, our rehabilitation team valuescompassion, collaboration, and clinical excellence. We work together to create individualized treatment plans and provide care that meets the unique needs of each resident and patient.

If you're looking for a supportive team where your clinical expertise can make a real difference, we'd love to hear from you

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and patients for speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans focused on cognition, communication, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech-language pathology services in accordance with established plans of care.
  • Help residents and patients achieve their individualized cognitive, communication, and swallowing goals.
  • Provide education, training, and support for residents, families, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals regarding diagnostic swallowing procedures, including Modified Barium Swallow Studies (MBSS) and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES), as ordered and clinically indicated.
  • Apply sound clinical judgment and maintain skills consistent with current speech-language pathology standards of practice.
  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

Speech-Language Pathologist Skills & Qualifications

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.
  • Familiarity with the Net Health electronic documentation system is preferred.
  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and patients with a variety of needs, abilities, and personalities.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, and the interdisciplinary team.
  • A genuine commitment to compassionate, patient-centered care.

Speech-Language Pathologist Requirements

  • Active and valid Speech-Language Pathology license inCA.
  • Current ASHA certification.
  • Must be in good standing with applicable licensing boards and regulatory agencies.

Why Join Our Team?

  • opportunity
  • In-house rehabilitation team
  • New graduates are welcome to apply
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Flexible scheduling
  • Supportive and collaborative clinical environment

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and patients for speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans focused on cognition, communication, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Provide skilled, medically necessary speech-language pathology services in accordance with established plans of care.
  • Help residents and patients achieve their individualized cognitive, communication, and swallowing goals.
  • Provide education, training, and support for residents, families, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.
  • Collaborate with physicians and other healthcare professionals regarding diagnostic swallowing procedures, including Modified Barium Swallow Studies (MBSS) and Fiberoptic Endoscopic Evaluation of Swallowing (FEES), as ordered and clinically indicated.
  • Apply sound clinical judgment and maintain skills consistent with current speech-language pathology standards of practice.
  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.

James L. West Alzheimer's Center

1111 Summit Avenue

Position Overview

James L. West Alzheimer's Center is seeking a compassionate, skilled, and dedicated Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our team on apart-time or per diem basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for an SLP who is passionate about providing person-centered care and helping individuals maintain their communication, swallowing, and functional abilities while supporting their dignity and quality of life.

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents to identify speech, language, cognitive-communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans based on each resident's clinical needs and goals.
  • Provide therapeutic interventions designed to improve communication, cognition, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Monitor resident progress and modify treatment plans as appropriate.
  • Complete accurate and timely clinical documentation in accordance with facility and regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with nursing, therapy, dietary, medical staff, families, and other members of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Educate residents, families, caregivers, and staff regarding communication strategies, swallowing precautions, and appropriate therapeutic techniques.
  • Promote resident safety, dignity, independence, and quality of life.
  • Provide compassionate, patient-centered care in a supportive environment.

Qualifications

  • Current and valid Speech-Language Pathologist license in the state of Texas.
  • Graduate of an accredited Speech-Language Pathology program.
  • Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC) through ASHA, as applicable.
  • Strong clinical, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with skilled nursing, long-term care, rehabilitation, geriatrics, or dementia care is preferred.
  • Experience working with individuals with Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia is a plus.
  • Compassionate and patient-centered approach to care.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary team.

Why Join James L. West Alzheimer's Center?

  • Part-time and per diem flexibility
  • Meaningful work serving individuals and families affected by Alzheimer's disease and dementia
  • Opportunity to make a direct impact on residents' communication, function, safety, and quality of life
  • Collaborative interdisciplinary care environment

  • Compassionate and patient-centered approach to care.

  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.

  • Strong clinical, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with skilled nursing, long-term care, rehabilitation, geriatrics, or dementia care is preferred.
  • Experience working with individuals with Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia is a plus.
  • Compassionate and patient-centered approach to care.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary team.

  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.

James L. West Alzheimer's Center

1111 Summit Avenue

Position Overview

James L. West Alzheimer's Center is seeking a compassionate, skilled, and dedicated Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our team on apart-time or per diem basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for an SLP who is passionate about providing person-centered care and helping individuals maintain their communication, swallowing, and functional abilities while supporting their dignity and quality of life.

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents to identify speech, language, cognitive-communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans based on each resident's clinical needs and goals.
  • Provide therapeutic interventions designed to improve communication, cognition, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Monitor resident progress and modify treatment plans as appropriate.
  • Complete accurate and timely clinical documentation in accordance with facility and regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with nursing, therapy, dietary, medical staff, families, and other members of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Educate residents, families, caregivers, and staff regarding communication strategies, swallowing precautions, and appropriate therapeutic techniques.
  • Promote resident safety, dignity, independence, and quality of life.
  • Provide compassionate, patient-centered care in a supportive environment.

Qualifications

  • Current and valid Speech-Language Pathologist license in the state of Texas.
  • Graduate of an accredited Speech-Language Pathology program.
  • Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC) through ASHA, as applicable.
  • Strong clinical, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with skilled nursing, long-term care, rehabilitation, geriatrics, or dementia care is preferred.
  • Experience working with individuals with Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia is a plus.
  • Compassionate and patient-centered approach to care.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary team.

Why Join James L. West Alzheimer's Center?

  • Part-time and per diem flexibility
  • Meaningful work serving individuals and families affected by Alzheimer's disease and dementia
  • Opportunity to make a direct impact on residents' communication, function, safety, and quality of life
  • Collaborative interdisciplinary care environment
  • Supportive team focused on person-centered care

Speech-Language Pathologist Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents and patients for speech, language, cognitive, communication, and swallowing needs.

  • Help residents and patients achieve their individualized cognitive, communication, and swallowing goals.
  • Provide education, training, and support for residents, families, caregivers, and other healthcare professionals.

  • Apply sound clinical judgment and maintain skills consistent with current speech-language pathology standards of practice.
  • Monitor progress and communicate changes in condition to the appropriate members of the healthcare team.
  • Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation and billing records in accordance with company policies and applicable requirements.
  • Respond to resident and family questions, requests, and concerns in a timely and professional manner.
  • Provide training and support to Restorative Nursing and other care staff.
  • Maintain resident and patient confidentiality and protect all personal health information.
  • Follow applicable federal, state, and local regulations, as well as professional standards and facility policies.
  • Attend required meetings and assist with other responsibilities as directed by the Director of Rehabilitation.

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.
  • Knowledge of current speech-language pathology treatment practices, techniques, and interventions.

  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and patients with a variety of needs, abilities, and personalities.
  • Strong organization and attention to detail.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with residents, families, caregivers, and the interdisciplinary team.
  • A genuine commitment to compassionate, patient-centered care.

  • Active and valid Speech-Language Pathology license inPA.
  • Current ASHA certification.
  • Must be in good standing with applicable licensing boards and regulatory agencies.

James L. West Alzheimer's Center

1111 Summit Avenue

Position Overview

James L. West Alzheimer's Center is seeking a compassionate, skilled, and dedicated Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our team on apart-time or per diem basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for an SLP who is passionate about providing person-centered care and helping individuals maintain their communication, swallowing, and functional abilities while supporting their dignity and quality of life.

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents to identify speech, language, cognitive-communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans based on each resident's clinical needs and goals.
  • Provide therapeutic interventions designed to improve communication, cognition, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Monitor resident progress and modify treatment plans as appropriate.
  • Complete accurate and timely clinical documentation in accordance with facility and regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with nursing, therapy, dietary, medical staff, families, and other members of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Educate residents, families, caregivers, and staff regarding communication strategies, swallowing precautions, and appropriate therapeutic techniques.
  • Promote resident safety, dignity, independence, and quality of life.
  • Provide compassionate, patient-centered care in a supportive environment.

Qualifications

  • Current and valid Speech-Language Pathologist license in the state of Texas.
  • Graduate of an accredited Speech-Language Pathology program.
  • Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC) through ASHA, as applicable.
  • Strong clinical, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with skilled nursing, long-term care, rehabilitation, geriatrics, or dementia care is preferred.
  • Experience working with individuals with Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia is a plus.
  • Compassionate and patient-centered approach to care.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary team.

Why Join James L. West Alzheimer's Center?

  • Part-time and per diem flexibility
  • Meaningful work serving individuals and families affected by Alzheimer's disease and dementia
  • Opportunity to make a direct impact on residents' communication, function, safety, and quality of life
  • Collaborative interdisciplinary care environment
  • Supportive team focused on person-centered care

James L. West Alzheimer's Center

1111 Summit Avenue

Position Overview

James L. West Alzheimer's Center is seeking a compassionate, skilled, and dedicated Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our team on apart-time or per diem basis.

This is an excellent opportunity for an SLP who is passionate about providing person-centered care and helping individuals maintain their communication, swallowing, and functional abilities while supporting their dignity and quality of life.

Key Responsibilities

  • Evaluate residents to identify speech, language, cognitive-communication, and swallowing needs.
  • Develop and implement individualized treatment plans based on each resident's clinical needs and goals.
  • Provide therapeutic interventions designed to improve communication, cognition, swallowing, and functional independence.
  • Monitor resident progress and modify treatment plans as appropriate.
  • Complete accurate and timely clinical documentation in accordance with facility and regulatory requirements.
  • Collaborate with nursing, therapy, dietary, medical staff, families, and other members of the interdisciplinary team.
  • Educate residents, families, caregivers, and staff regarding communication strategies, swallowing precautions, and appropriate therapeutic techniques.
  • Promote resident safety, dignity, independence, and quality of life.
  • Provide compassionate, patient-centered care in a supportive environment.

Qualifications

  • Current and valid Speech-Language Pathologist license in the state of Texas.
  • Graduate of an accredited Speech-Language Pathology program.
  • Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC) through ASHA, as applicable.
  • Strong clinical, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with skilled nursing, long-term care, rehabilitation, geriatrics, or dementia care is preferred.
  • Experience working with individuals with Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia is a plus.
  • Compassionate and patient-centered approach to care.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary team.

  • Part-time and per diem flexibility
  • Meaningful work serving individuals and families affected by Alzheimer's disease and dementia

  • Previous experience in a skilled nursing facility (SNF) or long-term care setting is preferred.

  • Strong clinical, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with residents and patients with a variety of needs, abilities, and personalities.

Position Overview

James L. West Alzheimer's Center is seeking a compassionate, skilled, and dedicated Speech-Language Pathologist (SLP) to join our team on apart-time or per diem basis.

  • Current and valid Speech-Language Pathologist license in the state of Texas.

  • Certificate of Clinical Competence (CCC) through ASHA, as applicable.
  • Strong clinical, communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.
  • Experience with skilled nursing, long-term care, rehabilitation, geriatrics, or dementia care is preferred.
  • Experience working with individuals with Alzheimer's disease or other forms of dementia is a plus.
  • Compassionate and patient-centered approach to care.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary team.
